title: Understand Percent · Part 2
note: GENERATED by scripts/generate-part-two.mjs from the core lesson — do not hand-edit.
contentObjective: I can explain a percent as a rate per 100, model it on a decimal grid or tape diagram, and interpret percents greater than 100%.
languageObjective: I can explain what a percent means using the words per hundred, part, whole, and equivalent ratio.

vocabulary.definition: A percent is a ratio that compares a number to 100, so every percent answers the question “how many out of 100?”
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un porcentaje es una razón que compara un número con 100, así que todo porcentaje responde “¿cuántos de cada 100?”
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio comparing a number to 100 is a ___.

examples.text: 65 shaded squares out of a 100-square grid is 65%
examples.why: It compares the part to a whole of exactly 100.
The whole is not 100, so the count is not the percent.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio that compares a number to 100. The word means “per hundred,” and the symbol is %.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara un número con 100. La palabra significa “por cada cien” y su símbolo es %.
vocabulary.cloze: The word that means “per hundred” is ___.

examples.text: 9 out of 100 students walk to school → 9%
examples.why: The comparison is already out of 100.
That is 90%, not 9% — both terms must be scaled to 100.

vocabulary.definition: The meaning hidden inside the word percent: for every group of 100. It is why every percent can be written as a fraction over 100.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El significado dentro de la palabra porcentaje: por cada grupo de 100. Por eso todo porcentaje se puede escribir como fracción sobre 100.
vocabulary.cloze: The meaning hidden inside the word percent is ___ ___.

examples.text: 3 out of every 10 rewritten as 30 out of 100
examples.why: It restates the ratio for a group of 100.

examples.text: 3 out of every 10 left as it is
examples.why: Until the whole is 100 you cannot read the percent off it.

vocabulary.definition: A 10-by-10 grid of 100 squares. Shading squares shows a percent directly, one square per percent.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cuadrícula de 10 por 10 con 100 cuadros. Sombrear cuadros muestra un porcentaje directamente, un cuadro por cada uno por ciento.
vocabulary.cloze: A 10-by-10 grid of 100 squares used to show a percent is a ___ ___.

examples.why: Each square is one percent, so the shading reads directly as 65%.

examples.text: A bar split into 8 unlabelled pieces
examples.why: Without 100 equal parts you cannot read a percent from it.

vocabulary.definition: A comparison of one part against the whole amount. In a percent, the whole is always 100%.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una comparación de una parte con el total. En un porcentaje, el total siempre es 100 %.
vocabulary.visual: The whole = 100%; the part = the percent
vocabulary.cloze: A comparison of one part against the whole amount is a ___ comparison.

examples.text: 18 students out of a class of 60
examples.why: The second number is the whole the part came from.
That compares two parts, not a part with its whole.

vocabulary.definition: More than one whole. A percent above 100 means the amount is larger than the thing it is being compared to.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Más de un entero. Un porcentaje mayor que 100 significa que la cantidad es mayor que aquello con lo que se compara.
vocabulary.visual: 150% of the gray kitten = 1.5 times its weight
vocabulary.cloze: A percent above 100 means the amount is ___ than one whole.

examples.why: One whole plus another half — more than the whole.
Half of one whole is less than the whole.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Car Sales
revealWordProblem.text:
A car dealership's sales for one month are shown in the monthly sales report. The owner now needs to order 50 cars from the factory.
Question: Based on the sales shown, how many of each type of car do you recommend the owner order?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A monthly sales report bar graph out of 100 cars sold: 8 hybrid, 18 all-electric, and 74 gas-powered.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Out of 100 cars sold, 8 were hybrid, 18 were all-electric, and 74 were gas-powered, so those counts are already percents: 8%, 18%, and 74%. Apply each percent to the 50-car order: 8% of 50 = 4 hybrids, 18% of 50 = 9 all-electric, and 74% of 50 = 37 gas-powered. That accounts for all 50 cars (4 + 9 + 37 = 50), so I recommend ordering 4, 9, and 37.

reviewCheck.stem: The orange kitten weighs 1.5 times as much as the gray kitten. What percent of the gray kitten's weight is that?
reviewCheck.explanation: The gray kitten is the whole, or 100%. One and a half wholes is 100% + 50% = 150%.
choiceFeedback: 15% would be a small fraction of the gray kitten, not more than all of it.
50% is only half the gray kitten's weight.
1.5% is a tiny sliver — but the orange kitten is heavier.
hints: One whole is 100%. What is half a whole?
Add the whole and the half.
reviewCheck.stemEs: El gatito anaranjado pesa 1.5 veces lo que pesa el gatito gris. ¿Qué porcentaje del peso del gatito gris es eso?
reviewCheck.explanationEs: El gatito gris es el entero, o 100%. Un entero y medio es 100% + 50% = 150%.
hintsEs: Un entero es 100%. ¿Cuánto es medio entero?
Suma el entero y la mitad.
